section: Science · Ch — Matter, Materials & Natural Resources
subject: Science
stem: Petroleum (crude oil), found trapped between rock layers deep underground, is separated in a refinery into several useful products (petrol, diesel, kerosene, LPG) based on their different boiling points. This separation process is called:
explanation: Fractional distillation heats crude oil so its components vaporise and separate at different boiling points, yielding distinct fractions (LPG, petrol, kerosene, diesel, and heavier products like lubricating oil and bitumen) — since petroleum is a fossil fuel, it is also a non-renewable resource.

section: Science · Ch — Matter, Materials & Natural Resources
subject: Science
stem: Many public buses and auto-rickshaws in Indian cities now run on a cleaner-burning fuel stored under high pressure in cylinders, mainly composed of methane, that produces significantly less air pollution than petrol or diesel. This fuel is called:
explanation: CNG, mainly methane compressed for storage, burns more cleanly than petrol/diesel and has been mandated for public transport in several major Indian cities to curb vehicular pollution — distinct from LPG (used mainly for cooking, a different hydrocarbon mixture).
